client.name: Example Pricing Co
client.offer: pricing and packaging advice for B2B software companies
client.why_signals_matter: a launch, new market, new owner or new leader is the moment a software company has to decide how to package and charge for something
client.sender: Alex Example, founder of Example Pricing Co

archetype.name: Archetype 1
archetype.description: B2B software company selling its own product on a subscription or licence model, 51-200 staff, founded in the last 5 years, not private-equity owned
disqualifiers: agencies, dev shops, IT services, MSPs, staffing
resellers and implementation partners of someone else's software
companies being absorbed into their buyer (product shut down or folded in)

grading.A: B2B software/SaaS with a subscription or licence model visible on the site (public tiers, per user, usage/credits, or a pricing page that says contact sales for plans)
grading.B: own B2B tech product, but the pricing model is not visible, or product plus a large services arm
grading.C: borderline: mostly services with a small product, customer base unclear, or the site could not be read
grading.DROP: anything in the disqualifiers list, or a dead site

signals.name: new product or module launched
signals.not_a_signal: a feature, an integration or connector, a point release, a beta or waitlist

signals.name: AI feature, agent or copilot launched, or an AI add-on priced
signals.not_a_signal: a blog post about AI, a 'coming soon' page

signals.name: new country or new market entered
signals.not_a_signal: a single customer abroad, a reseller agreement

signals.name: pricing model or published price change
funding round closed
signals.not_a_signal: a partner 'commitment', an unfinished bid, a grant application

signals.name: acquired, merged or PE-invested while still trading under its own brand
signals.not_a_signal: the company is being absorbed into its buyer's product or brand

signals.name: new CEO, CRO, CCO, CFO or VP Pricing appointed
signals.not_a_signal: a promotion below the commercial leadership, a board seat

signals.name: open role for pricing, RevOps, monetisation, CRO or CCO

proof.line: REPLACE: one real, client-approved result, e.g. 15% more revenue from a targeted price increase, no key accounts lost
proof.solves: raising prices on an existing base without losing customers; renewals; fear of churn

proof.line: REPLACE: e.g. conversion up 17% and new customers up 10% after replacing a single price with clear tiers
proof.solves: packaging: what is in the base plan and what is paid extra; a new module that needs a place in the plans

proof.line: REPLACE: e.g. won a six-figure deal after revising its product and pricing offer
proof.solves: pricing a new or AI product so its first big deals land

rules: facts only: the opener states the dated event, nothing else
never judge or describe the prospect's pricing; scraped pricing data is internal only
no links, no images, no tracking pixel in email one
no em dashes, no exclamation marks, no praise words, no congratulations
write company names as people say them (Builder, not Builder.io)

sending.optout_text: If you would rather I did not write again, just reply and say so.
